title: Relative object descent for finite Hilbert groupoids
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of stacks in groupoids on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and object descent is effective. Suppose $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}h_T$ is an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. Assume each $X_y\to T$ is locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every integer $d\geq1$, the map $p_d:\mathcal H_d(F)\to\mathcal Y$ [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids] has the following relative object-descent property. Let $(T_i)$ be any small nonempty directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes with limit $T$ and affine transition maps. Given an index $i$, an object $y_i\in\mathcal Y(T_i)$, an object $\xi\in\mathcal H_d(F)(T)$ and an isomorphism $\gamma:p_d(\xi)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_T$, there exist $j\geq i$, $\xi_j\in\mathcal H_d(F)(T_j)$ and isomorphisms $a:\xi_j|_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\xi$, $b:p_d(\xi_j)\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i|_{T_j}$ with $b|_T=\gamma\circ p_d(a)$. No flatness or surjectivity of $F$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06CH (lemma-limit-preserving), with relative object-descent terminology of Tag 06CX (lemma-representable-by-spaces-limit-preserving).

proof.text: Restrict the index set to $J=\{j:j\geq i\}$. This remains small, nonempty and directed and has the same limit $T$, now viewed over $T_i$. Indeed a cone on the tail extends to an index $k$ by choosing $j\geq i,k$ and composing its map to $T_j$ with $T_j\to T_k$; a common upper bound proves independence and compatibility. This construction is inverse to restricting cones. We henceforth work on this tail.

source.place: Tag 06CH (lemma-limit-preserving), initial limit datum; elementary verification of restriction to the tail

proof.text: Write $\xi=(Z\to T,y,x,\alpha)$ using [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. Set $\delta=\alpha\circ(\gamma|_Z)^{-1}:y_i|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$. Replacing $(y,\alpha)$ by $(y_i|_T,\delta)$ gives an object $\xi'$ and an isomorphism $c:\xi'\to\xi$ with cover map $\mathrm{id}_Z$, $x$-component $\mathrm{id}_x$ and $y$-component $\gamma^{-1}$: its arrow equation is $\delta=\alpha\circ\gamma^{-1}|_Z$. Let $W=X_{y_i}$, locally finitely presented over $T_i$ by hypothesis. By the explicit represented-fibre convention of [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids], the assumed representation identifies the fibre groupoid of pairs $(v,\epsilon:y_i|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}F(v))$ with the discrete groupoid $W(V)$, naturally for $V\to T_i$. Thus $(x,\delta)$ gives a point of $W(Z)$, or equivalently a map $u:Z\to W$ by [lem-pc-yoneda] and the sheaf convention [def-trf-algebraic-space]. This uses the given equivalence of fibred groupoids evaluated at $Z$, rather than an assertion about coarse isomorphism classes alone.

source.place: Tag 06CH (lemma-limit-preserving), representing space and the map f_xi; explicit normalization of the prescribed comparison

proof.text: The cover $Z\to T$ is finite, flat and locally finitely presented by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The limit $T$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Affine schemes are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $T$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b) makes $Z$ affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) its locally finitely presented structure map to the affine scheme $T$ is of finite presentation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-family-descent] to the one-member family $Z\to T$ and the tail system: all its bases are affine, hence qcqs, and its transition maps are affine. Obtain a finite-presentation qcqs scheme $Z_k\to T_k$ and a $T$-isomorphism $\lambda:Z_k\times_{T_k}T\xrightarrow{\sim}Z$, with $k\geq i$.

source.place: Tag 06CH (lemma-limit-preserving), descent of the cover, first application of limits.tex Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] to the tail based at $k$, with $S_0=T_k$, $X_0=Z_k$, $Y_0=T_k$ and $f_0$ the structure map. These three schemes are qcqs, $f_0$ is locally finitely presented, and its limit base change is the given finite locally free cover of degree $d$ via $\lambda$. We obtain $l\geq k$ such that $Z_l=Z_k\times_{T_k}T_l\to T_l$ is finite locally free of degree $d$. For $j\geq l$ put $Z_j=Z_l\times_{T_l}T_j$. Finiteness, flatness and local finite presentation persist by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3); degree stays $d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso](2). The $Z_j$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](b). By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit], this small directed system has affine transition maps and limit $Z_l\times_{T_l}T\simeq Z$.

source.place: Tag 06CH (lemma-limit-preserving), descent of the cover with degree d, limits.tex Tag 06AC; formation of its base-change system

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-lfp-space-scheme-limit-test] over the base scheme $T_i$ to $W\to T_i$ and $(Z_j)_{j\geq l}$. Its source schemes are affine, in particular qcqs, its transitions are affine, and its limit is identified with $Z$ in step 4. The representing map is locally finitely presented by the hypothesis on $F$. The factorization clause gives $j\geq l$ and a $T_i$-map $u_j:Z_j\to W$ whose restriction, under $\lambda$, equals $u$. There is no need for $W$ to be quasi-compact or quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 06CH (lemma-limit-preserving), factorization of f_xi through Z_j, spaces-limits.tex Tag 04AK

proof.text: Evaluate the representing equivalence of [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids] at $Z_j$. The point $u_j$ gives $x_j\in\mathcal X(Z_j)$ and $\alpha_j:y_i|_{Z_j}\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x_j)$, so $\xi_j=(Z_j\to T_j,y_i|_{T_j},x_j,\alpha_j)$ is a Hilbert object by [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. Naturality sends its restriction to $u_j|_Z=u$. Full faithfulness of the equivalence with a discrete groupoid therefore lifts this equality to an isomorphism $\eta:x_j|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}x$ satisfying $F(\eta)\circ\alpha_j|_Z=\delta$. With the cover identification $\lambda$ and identity on $y_i|_T$, this is precisely a Hilbert arrow $c':\xi_j|_T\to\xi'$. Set $a=c\circ c'$ and let $b:p_d(\xi_j)\to y_i|_{T_j}$ be the identity. Then $p_d(a)=\gamma^{-1}$, so $\gamma\circ p_d(a)=\mathrm{id}=b|_T$. The displayed equation also checks the $x$-component of the arrow to $\xi$, since $F(\eta)\alpha_j=\alpha\gamma^{-1}|_Z$. Thus both requested isomorphisms and their compatibility are obtained.
